findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture row at its foot ('Streamlining the PPP Process… Lecture · 23 April 2026', with a download arrow and 'PDF')
findings.fault: The row shows a download arrow and the word PDF, so it promises a file. But the whole row links to #article, which only jumps back to the top of the article the visitor has just read. No file downloads.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who wants Mark's lecture to read offline or pass on to a colleague. They click PDF, the page scrolls up, and they get no file and no reason why. The research calls the PDF list 'the product', so a dead download damages the depth that should build trust.

findings.fault: All three nav items go to the same place, #article. 'Profile' therefore opens a blog post about PPP law, not anything about Mark. Three labels that promise three different places all land on one.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor checking who Mark is before they write to him. They click Profile to see his background and land in the middle of an article. The name and the profile are the personal-advisor test, and this nav item fails it.

findings.where: Header lockup, the name 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the mark
findings.fault: The mark next to the name is a link home, but the name is static text. It sits in the same lockup, set off by its own divider, so it looks like part of the home link and does nothing when clicked.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a deeper page who clicks the name, as on most personal sites, to get back home. Nothing happens. The brief makes his name lead the lockup, so it is the part people will reach for first.

findings.where: Article specimen, the blue numbers on the three-item list (the palette's 'list numbers' row confirms it)
findings.fault: The list numbers use the house blue, which the page reserves for links. The tile's own note says 'blue only where something can be clicked', yet these numbers are static.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the article, which is the surface Angélique will fill most often. They learn on this page that blue means 'click', then meet blue that does nothing. Each time she adds a list, the rule the page itself states gets weaker.

findings.fault: It is a button that acts in place, but it is styled exactly like a navigation link: blue, underlined, with no edge or fill. It also does not say which opening it replays, the preview above it or the hero at the top of the page.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the motion. They expect the link to take them somewhere and are unsure what will move. A button dressed as a link takes on a look the page reserves for navigation.
